evidence_items.locator: Section Why Are Companies Cutting?, final paragraph

receipt.public_excerpt: Artificial Intelligence was the fifth-most cited reason with 3,961 cuts in September, about 9% of the month’s total.

evidence_items.explanation: The report also records 120,136 AI-cited announcements through September, making the layoff concern material. These are announcements attributed broadly to AI, not verified completed dismissals caused by the generative AI bubble or its collapse.

evidence_items.locator: Paragraph following the discussion of municipal water infrastructure upgrades

receipt.public_excerpt: Such improvements will be needed at a time when many public water systems are aging and financially constrained, the report says.

evidence_items.explanation: The university's account of its researchers' study identifies infrastructure pressure from AI and cloud-computing growth. Projected capacity needs do not establish realized, lasting environmental and infrastructure chaos attributable specifically to generative AI.

receipt.public_excerpt: AI captured 80%+ of venture capital through Q3 2026 while many startups face selective funding.

evidence_items.explanation: Continued concentration of venture funding in AI cautions against declaring the predicted collapse established. This broader funding measure neither measures a Silicon Valley depression nor rules out a future collapse.

unresolved_gaps: No verified count establishes completed layoffs attributable to the predicted boom-and-collapse mechanism.
The reviewed environmental source projects infrastructure requirements rather than establishing the claimed lasting chaos.
No admitted evidence establishes a Silicon Valley downturn substantially worse than the dot-com bust on consistent measures.
The forecast supplies no deadline or duration for observing its full consequences.
